full_block_review.assessment: Interference and diffraction are evidence of wave behavior, not an assertion that light has no other physical description. Both explain meeting waves and spreading at openings or obstacles.

Soap bubbles and kerosene/petroleum films are retained. Mark Twain is the source's actual named identity. The quoted passage is literary source material, not a scientific assertion that thin-film colors merely copy surrounding objects. The English companion reason explicitly calls the wording a translation of the supplied Chinese source, not a recovered original English quotation; the learner text attributes it to the textbook and makes no restoration claim.

Wave 1 reflects at the outer surface; wave 2 enters the film, reflects internally and emerges. Figure 198 and all six source math tokens are retained in order. Phase is explained as progress through a cycle. Propagation and reflection contributions are included in total phase, and effective delay is explicitly an equivalent distance, not raw geometric path difference. Under the stated near-normal transparent nonabsorbing interface model, lower-to-higher-index reflection reverses the oscillation by half a cycle and the reverse direction does not. Equal frequency, aligned oscillation directions, fixed observation point and stable phase relation limit the integer-wavelength strengthening and odd-half-wavelength weakening rules. Complete cancellation additionally requires equal amplitudes. The source-attributed Young priority statement remains attributed to the textbook.
Text-only slot identity and empty source snapshot retained. No SCI, FIG, display or asset assessment is assigned to this empty image slot.
Source caption remains a separate block. Figure number 198 is unchanged; Figure 198 is the supported English localization of the numbered caption.

Same-medium wavelength comparison and equal frequency are linked correctly. Coherence requires a constant relative phase, not necessarily zero phase. Same-beam splitting is not presented as an unconditional guarantee: limited path difference and stable film/path geometry are stated. Ordinary independent sources lack a stable relative phase and their changing interference contributions average out during normal observation.

Color is related to frequency and to wavelength when the comparison medium is specified. Frequency preservation at an interface is correct in the ordinary stationary-media context of this lesson; speed and wavelength can change. This is not an assessment of moving interfaces or frequency-converting media. White light has multiple spectral components. Each color's two reflected components interfere; the text does not claim that waves of different frequencies cancel one another. Different film thicknesses select different reinforcement/weakening combinations, including reflection phase changes.
Retains the backward reference to the previous unit and introduces the deeper physical dispersion definition without importing n85 or a color-plate reference.

Dispersion is refractive-index dependence on frequency or appropriately specified wavelength, not just the visual act of splitting colors. Refractive index is connected to propagation speed. Both distinguish a medium-induced wavelength change from a color change and explain how index differences can produce different refraction angles.

Thomas Young's identity, British nationality, dates 1773-1829, medicine, physics, astronomy, mechanical engineering, metallurgy, Egyptology, physiology, languages, music and gymnastics are retained. The account is framed as the supplied textbook's history, and the two specialist fields are explained for younger readers.

Text-only portrait slot and empty source snapshot are retained in the original assembled position. Its descriptive labels change the source-bound null label; see the data-contract finding. No portrait pixels, identity likeness, generation, FIG or display assessment was performed.

Retains the source's credit to Young for interference, the term interference, wave-based diffraction explanation and the first light-wavelength measurement. Both distinguish scientific discovery/explanation from people already seeing bubble or oil-film colors, avoiding an internal historical contradiction.

child_causal_clarity.assessment: The explanation follows a usable causal chain for an 8-12-year-old reading the lesson: familiar film colors; two reflected waves; stronger/weaker combined oscillation; phase as a stage of a cycle; propagation and reflection effects; stable relative phase; different wavelengths responding differently to thickness; dispersion as index dependence. Frequency, phase, effective delay and the specialist biographical fields receive local explanations. The total-phase bookkeeping is demanding but is qualified and explained in both languages, not hidden inside a memorized geometric-distance rule.
child_causal_clarity.limits: Text judgment only, not a child user study or display assessment. Differing paragraph counts do not change semantic content.
